about: Advanced Placement at Lunenburg High, SY2007 to SY2025: who sits the exams, in what subjects, and how the tests score.

conclusions.basis: `dese_ap` participation, Lunenburg district, All Students, All Subjects; `dese_enrollment` grades 11 and 12 for the denominator.
conclusions.claim: 89 students sat at least one AP exam in SY2025 — about 39% of the 11th and 12th grades.
conclusions.detail: A smaller high school sends a larger share of its upperclassmen into AP exams than it did. 89 students took 154 exams in SY2025, against 227 in the 11th and 12th grades. In SY2007 it was 58 students against 322. The ratio is an approximation: a tenth grader can sit an exam, and the two DESE files count on different days.

takers.unit: students sat an AP exam, SY2025

conclusions.not_shown: Who is offered the courses, who is steered toward or away from the exam, or what a sitting costs a family. Participation is a count of who sat.
conclusions.so_what: In SY2007 it was 18% of a bigger class. The count peaked at 122 in SY2018.

conclusions.basis: `dese_ap` performance, Lunenburg district, All Students, All Subjects, pct_3_5 and the score counts.
conclusions.claim: 88.3% of AP tests scored 3 or better in SY2025, the best of 19 years; the low: 62.1% in SY2009.
conclusions.detail: Of 154 tests in SY2025, 28 scored a five and 2 scored a one; the full distribution is charted below. It is a share of TESTS, not of students: a student who sat three exams counts three times.
conclusions.not_shown: Why. Better teaching, different students choosing to sit, or the mix of subjects shifting toward ones with higher pass rates all produce this number, and the file separates none of them.
conclusions.so_what: A score of 3 is the usual threshold for college credit. Two years ago it was 75.8%.

conclusions.basis: `dese_ap` participation, subject-family rollups (DESE’s own, `subj = subj_cat`), Lunenburg district, SY2015 and SY2025.
conclusions.claim: 117 of 154 AP sittings in SY2025 were English or history; science and math were 31.
conclusions.detail: 76% of sittings in SY2025 were in English or history. The table below gives every subject family at both ends. This is the exam-room view of what /what-courses-actually-ran measures in the schedule: a language programme narrowing, and a STEM one that sits few exams.
conclusions.not_shown: Whether the courses are offered and unchosen, or not offered. A sitting count cannot tell a closed door from an empty room. Small families are suppressed in DESE’s participation file and taken from its performance file, which says so in the table.

see.label: Foreign language, narrowing on every instrument

conclusions.so_what: In SY2015 science and math were 51 sittings. Foreign languages: 22 then, 1 now.

grain: Three counts that are not the same thing: CHILDREN who sat at least one exam, SITTINGS, and TESTS at each score. The participation ratio divides children by the 11th and 12th grade enrolment and is an approximation.
not_established: Which AP courses the high school offers in a given year; DESE counts exams sat, not courses taught.
Anything about the students who did not sit: whether they were in the course and chose not to, or never had access.
How Lunenburg compares to other districts — the extract holds Lunenburg only.
